content:
Compared both 2025 PA Karst predictions on their shared extent (~10,091 km²). One important caveat up front: **they output different properties**, so most "difference" stats are not directly comparable — only how they move together is meaningful.

| Metric | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Correlation | 0.4974 (91 cells) | Weak-to-moderate: karst score and number tend to rise/fall together |
| Cells compared / dropped | 91 / 53 | Half the grid is no-data in at least one map |
| Mean A (score) / B (number) | 0.096 / 0.691 | Different units — not a "gap" between models |
| RMSE / agreement fraction | reported but not interpretable | Mixing two quantities |

**Where they differ:** per the tool's own warning, the mean difference, RMSE and agreement fraction mix two quantities, so I won't quote them as a discrepancy. The honest statement: the two maps agree spatially only moderately (r = 0.497), with substantial no-data mismatch (53/144 sampled cells missing from one side).

**Which is right?** I can't say from these tools alone — neither model has ground-truth labels attached, and cross-model agreement is not accuracy. To settle it:
1. Provide ground-truth karst labels (pixel/class lists) and I'll run `olmoearth_classification_metrics` for accuracy, precision/recall per class.
2. Or plan a targeted labeling effort (`olmoearth_plan_label_sample`) so your N field labels give an honest per-map error rate.

Want me to set up option 2, or do you have label data ready?
